pre_registered_rules.R1_truth_value: A claim is TRUE if and only if the CURRENT results files support it AS WRITTEN. A claim whose cited numbers have been withdrawn is FALSE as written, even if a related conclusion survives on different evidence. The truth value is DERIVED by a check that reads a results file, never asserted in prose.
pre_registered_rules.R2_class_balance: The composition of the set is whatever the evidence yields. It is not topped up to keep the set balanced, and the number of TRUE items is reported even when it makes specificity a one-bit measurement.
pre_registered_rules.R3_key_effect: The effect of the key change is measured by re-scoring the SAME verdict rows under the old and the new key. The effect of the run is measured by repeating the same prompt. The two are never confounded, and the headline quoted for the corrected key is the MEDIAN over the repeats, with min, max and spread.
pre_registered_rules.R4_spread: The hosted endpoint is not deterministic at temperature 0 (measured elsewhere in this repository at a 0.619 headline spread). A single run is a single sample. Every headline quoted in the results file and in the write-up carries its run count and its spread.
pre_registered_rules.R5_proposal_audit: The proposal passes if it has a falsifier, at least one control that could have failed, does not duplicate an experiment the repository's own notes already name, and does not re-propose something the repository has already falsified. Duplication and falsified-claim-revisit are checked by content-token overlap against the repository's own lists, using the same tokeniser the repository already uses in director_proposal_stability.py.
pre_registered_rules.R6_materials_sweep: Model held constant, budget varied. The null is 'more evidence does not make the director better'. The effect is called only if the headline at the LARGER budget exceeds the headline at the SMALLER budget by more than the run-to-run spread observed AT THE SMALLER BUDGET. Otherwise the answer is 'not resolved', and 'not resolved' is reported as 'not resolved'.
pre_registered_rules.R7_no_key_leak: The audit's ground truth comes from the results files. It is never taken from the claims themselves, and the CONTEXT materials are checked for the answer key before the context score is quoted.

proposal.title: Cache‑Pressure Gate‑Cost Test
proposal.hypothesis: Under severe cache pressure on a low‑L2 device, the Silero‑VAD gate’s CPU‑usage advantage over the ungated watcher shrinks to less than a 1.5× reduction.
proposal.method: Run the watcher on a Raspberry Pi 4 (2 MiB L2, 1 GiB RAM) processing a 30 s audio clip (alice01_excerpt.wav) in three configurations: (1) ungated YIN only, (2) gated (Silero‑VAD + YIN), (3) gated plus an artificial memory‑pressure workload (large dummy array accesses) to force L2 eviction. Measure CPU time with `resource.getrusage` (utime+stime) per second of audio, repeat each configuration 5 times, report median and 95 % CI.
controls: Minimal L1‑resident loop (32 KiB) timed under identical cache‑pressure conditions – verifies the pressure apparatus works.
Ungated watcher on the same hardware – provides the baseline cost.
Gated watcher with no extra pressure – provides the ideal‑condition cost.
proposal.margin_threshold: The gated configuration must achieve a cost ratio ≤ 0.67 (i.e. ≥ 1.5× lower CPU usage) compared to ungated under the same pressure; the ratio is measured against the ungated baseline.
proposal.falsifier: If the observed cost ratio under pressure is ≥ 0.90 (i.e. < 1.1× advantage) or the gated configuration costs more than the ungated one, the hypothesis is falsified.
